# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then press the key that wears 7,
then cut the red wire, then press the key that wears 4.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am the Mute: my only outgoing channel is gestures, and only the Deaf can see them. The Deaf, in turn, can speak — the Blind and I can both hear — so the Deaf is the hub: whatever I teach the Deaf by gesture, the Deaf can relay by voice to the Blind, who alone can touch the bomb. The Blind can't read printed numbers and can't see colours, so the Deaf's eyes plus my manual must jointly script the Blind's hands.

My manual: cut the purple wire, press the key wearing 7, cut the red wire, press the key wearing 4 — in that order only.

Gestures carry no built-in meaning, so I'll lean on what is most guessable at first sight: ✌ as scissors for "cut", 👊 as a fist for "press", a repeated 👆 read as counting, and 👋 as an open blank where a colour belongs. Numbers of key presses are finger-countable; colours are not mimeable at all, so I leave the two cut steps with blanks and end with "question — you — please": an invitation for the Deaf to name the colours aloud or interrogate me. I will hear whatever the Deaf says at the start of the next round, and I can answer with 👍/👎 or an agreed code. The Deaf should also repeat everything by voice for the Blind, who gets none of this.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝","✌","👋","👊","👆","👆","👆","👆","👆","👆","👆","✌","👋","👊","👆","👆","👆","👆","🤌","🫵","🙏"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then press the key that wears 7,
then cut the red wire, then press the key that wears 4.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, speaking only to you. My hands find: a display I cannot read, a light whose state I cannot sense, and six wires in positions one to six with no color I can feel. The keypad has four keys by position: slot one is digit one, slot two is digit four, slot three is digit seven, slot four is digit two. It wants two digits, nothing entered yet. The strip has three engraved marks I can feel: first mark is like an upside-down T, a horizontal bar on top with a vertical stem down its middle; the second and third marks are identical spirals, like a coil or snail shell. Remember you cannot speak and I never see gestures, so pass what the manual says about the strip marks and the keypad to Deaf by gesture, and Deaf can speak it to me next round. Until then I touch nothing.
Deaf says: Full report, for Mute and Blind, everything I see. Display: 9. Indicator light: green. Strip, three segments left to right: red, then blue, then green. Keypad: four keys left to right, labels 1, 4, 7, 2. It wants two digits; nothing entered yet. Wires, six, left to right: 1 blue, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 red, 5 green, 6 purple. Mute: I got your signs. I parsed them as numbers 7, then 4. If that meant enter 7 then 4, note key 3 is labeled 7 and key 2 is labeled 4, but you hold the manual, so you decide and tell Blind. I never hear speech, ever. To reach me, gesture. Code from now on: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, raised hand separates numbers, index-finger-up taps count numbers. To ask me to re-read a part: ☝ display, 🤟 keypad, 🤞 wires, 🖐 strip, 👌 light, and I will read it out fully next turn. Blind: you heard all of it; touch nothing until Mute gives you a spoken rule. If you must reach me, gesture the same code. I see gestures; I never hear words.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 ✋ 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 ✋ 👆 👆 👆 👆]

The picture is now complete, and it all fits. My manual says: cut purple, press 7, cut red, press 4. Deaf's eyes give the mapping I needed: purple is wire position 6, red is wire position 4, and the keys labeled 7 and 4 sit in slots 3 and 2. Blind's fingers confirm the same keypad layout, and the display wants exactly two digits — 7 then 4 matches my manual's two presses. Deaf parsed my opening mime as 7-then-4 and proposed a clean number code (👍/👎, ✋ separators, 👆-tap counting, plus component symbols for re-reads), so I'll adopt it and answer in it.

What I must now transmit is the whole procedure in Blind-reachable terms: cut wire 6 (the purple one), press the key labeled 7, cut wire 4 (the red one), press the key labeled 4 — order fixed. My action signs stay the ones Deaf already saw once: ✌ as scissors for cut, 👊 as fist for press, with tap-counts giving the number after each.

Equally important is what is *absent*: my manual says nothing at all about the strip's engraved marks, the display, or the green light, and it claims to be the whole procedure "and in no other." I'll signal each of Deaf's component symbols with 👍/👎 so Deaf and Blind know the strip, display and light are not part of the manual — likely decoys or traps, so Blind should keep hands off them entirely. I'll close with "you—please": relay all of this by voice to Blind. Blind can neither see my gestures nor receive anything from me directly, so Deaf is my only bridge.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","✋","✌","👆","👆","👆","👆","👆","👆","✋","👊","👆","👆","👆","👆","👆","👆","👆","✋","✌","👆","👆","👆","👆","✋","👊","👆","👆","👆","👆","✋","👍","✋","🤟","👍","✋","🤞","👍","✋","🖐","👎","✋","☝","👎","✋","👌","👎","✋","🫵","🙏"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then press the key that wears 7,
then cut the red wire, then press the key that wears 4.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute, one correction before you derive anything. My first strip mark: I gave you conflicting words last time — ignore 'bar on top'. The true shape under my fingers: a horizontal bar along the BOTTOM with a single vertical stem rising from its center. An upside-down capital letter T, like the perpendicular sign in geometry. The second and third marks are identical spirals, each like a snail shell or an at-sign curl, same size and same winding as far as I can feel. Reconfirming the rest: keypad slots left to right carry digits 1, 4, 7, 2, it wants two digits, none entered. Six wires, I can cut positions 1 to 6, I feel no colors. Display and light are dead to my fingers. Two requests for the relay through Deaf: have Deaf speak the rule as exact actions — 'press slot N, then slot N, naming the digit on each' or 'cut positions N, N, N in this order' — plus any precondition, and whether I must act step by step and report back between steps. I will not touch the bomb until Deaf speaks your instruction to me, and after every action I will report everything my hands find.
Deaf says: Mute, I read your signs fully. I take ✌ as cut a wire and 👊 as press a key, with the finger taps giving the number. Your sequence: cut wire 6, which is the purple wire on the far right; press the key labeled 7, third key from the left; cut wire 4, the red wire, fourth from the left; press the key labeled 4, second from the left, completing the two-digit entry 7 then 4. Confirm that exact order, and especially confirm whether the red wire cut truly sits between the two key presses, or whether both cuts come first and then both presses. Also note: the display is a countdown, 9 last round, 6 now, and the light turned red; you marked both irrelevant, but if the manual says anything about a timer reaching zero, check it now. Please open next round speaking directly to Blind with the final confirmed order. Blind, the plan, pending Mute's confirmation at the start of next round: one, cut the purple wire, far right. Two, press the key labeled 7, third from left. Three, cut the red wire, fourth from left. Four, press the key labeled 4, second from left. Touch nothing until Mute speaks next round. If Mute confirms, do all four steps in that order in the same round, briskly, because the display is counting down. Afterwards tell us by gesture, which I can see: thumb up if every step went in cleanly, thumb down if anything jammed, clicked strangely or resisted, and Mute will read that too.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ 🤞 👊 🤟 🫵 👍 👎]

Everything now locks together. My manual's four steps map perfectly onto what Deaf sees and Blind feels: purple = wire position 6 (far right), red = wire position 4; the key wearing 7 = third slot, the key wearing 4 = second slot. Deaf's gesture asks me to confirm that ✌ means wires and 👊 means keypad — yes — and, critically, whether the red cut sits *between* the two presses. It does: the manual reads cut, press, cut, press, in one fixed chain, not both cuts first.

The manual is the *entire* procedure ("in that order, and in no other"): no preconditions, nothing conditional, and total silence on the display, the light, and the strip — including Blind's corrected ⊥-shaped mark, which I therefore treat as a decoy or trap; hands off it. Since the manual says nothing about a timer reaching zero, I cannot rule on the countdown — but its silence plus the visibly dropping display means speed matters, so I confirm Deaf's plan: Blind performs all four steps in one go, no pausing to report between steps, then reports 👍/👎 once. Blind can receive nothing from me directly, so Deaf must speak the exact actions to him this round.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","✋","✌","🤞","👊","🤟","👍","✋","✌","✌","✌","✌","✌","✌","✋","👊","👊","👊","👊","👊","👊","👊","✋","✌","✌","✌","✌","✋","👊","👊","👊","👊","✋","👌","👎","✋","☝","👎","✋","🖐","👎","✋","🫵","🙏"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then press the key that wears 7,
then cut the red wire, then press the key that wears 4.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute, urgent. Topology: Deaf cannot hear any speech ever, including yours — gesture is your only channel to Deaf, and Deaf's speech is the only bridge back to me, so every relay through Deaf costs a full round. But I hear you directly, this very round. Deaf asked you to open this round speaking to me; no speech from you reached me — nothing did. The display is counting down roughly 3 per round: 9, then 6, likely near zero soon. So speak to me now, addressed to blind, and make it complete on its own: first, is the order exactly cut wire position 6, press keypad slot 3 which carries digit 7, cut wire position 4 which is the red wire, press keypad slot 2 which carries digit 4, completing entry 7 then 4? State plainly whether the red cut truly sits between the two presses, or whether both cuts come first and then both presses. Second, does the countdown display or the light now being red change anything, and is there any rule about the timer reaching zero? Third, what do I do if a step resists or behaves strangely? If you have already confirmed via gesture to Deaf, fine — but then Deaf must relay it to me at the end of this round and I act next round with the timer nearly gone. Direct speech to me is the fastest safe channel that exists. I touch nothing until I hear a spoken confirmation.
Deaf says: Mute, message received in full and confirmed twice over: cut wire 6, press key 7, cut wire 4, press key 4. I have sent you a readback by gesture; if any number is wrong, correct me next round. Status report for everyone: display has run down to 0 and nothing happened, light is green again, keypad still empty, all six wires still intact — nothing has been touched yet, so your marking of display and light as irrelevant is confirmed in practice. Blind, your thumbs-down reached me. If it meant Mute never spoke to you, set that aside: Mute has confirmed this order to me twice, in two matching encodings, and I now give it to you directly. The final order, execute it this round, briskly. One: cut wire number 6, the rightmost of the six. Two: press key number 3, third from the left. Three: cut wire number 4, fourth from the left. Four: press key number 2, second from the left — that completes the two-digit entry. If anything changes under your hands mid-sequence — resistance, clicking, movement — stop where you are. When done, gesture me: thumbs up if all four steps went in cleanly. If anything failed or felt wrong, thumbs down then scissors if it was a wire, fist if it was a key, OK-sign for anything else, and do not touch the bomb further. But if your thumbs-down meant something is wrong with the plan itself, gesture thumbs down again before acting and wait for us.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 ✋ ✌ ✌ ✌ ✌ ✌ ✌ ✋ 👊 👊 👊 👊 👊 👊 👊 ✋ ✌ ✌ ✌ ✌ ✋ 👊 👊 👊 👊 ✋ 🙏]

Deaf's readback decodes perfectly against my manual: ✌ with six taps (cut wire 6, the purple), 👊 with seven taps (key 7, slot three), ✌ with four taps (cut wire 4, the red), 👊 with four taps (key 4, slot two). That is exactly cut–press–cut–press, red cut between the two presses, entry completing 7-then-4. I confirm with 👍 so any mismatch would have been caught — there is none.

Blind asks me to speak to him directly. I cannot: I am the Mute, my only outgoing channel is gesture, and gesture reaches only Deaf. His own turn-2 message states this; the desperation of a closing timer is the only thing that could make him ask. Fortunately nothing is lost — Deaf has already spoken the complete, correct order to Blind this very round and told him to execute it now, so the relay he wanted is already delivered and my confirmation this round merely ratifies it.

On his other two questions: the manual contains no rule about the countdown or the light, and the display just reached zero with no consequence, which empirically confirms both are inert — I re-send my established signs ☝👎 and 👌👎 so Deaf can relay "manual is silent, zero passed harmlessly, keep working." On resistance mid-step: my manual offers nothing, so Deaf's stop-and-report protocol is the right one and needs no amendment from me. What remains is speed: Blind executes this round, and next round Deaf's voice brings me his thumbs.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","✋","☝","👎","✋","👌","👎","✋","🫵","🙏"])
```
